rows.basis:
Everything ties except one item on the final frame.

Frame 1 is effectively the same picture in both labels (mean absolute RGB difference 0.13/255), so f001 contributes nothing. Divergence grows to 2.55 at f049 and 8.14 at f097. Mean RGB is within 1 level between labels at every frame, so no brightness/warmth confound entered any of these judgements.

Q1 ties 6/6/6 both labels. The six are: left foreground operator, mid-left operator, far mid-left seated figure, standing man in the aisle, mid-right seated figure, right foreground operator. Nobody is lost or added in either label at any frame. The two fogged mid-distance figures degrade to head-and-shoulders behind a chair by f097 in BOTH labels, to about the same degree; if anything A's mid-right figure keeps a slightly more readable arm and A's mid-left a slightly rounder head, but that is a high-zoom-only difference in heavy backlit fog.

Q2 ties at every frame. I counted the lower row of the right-hand bank in two fixed windows at 9x. The count falls with the push-in (14 -> 13 -> 11) identically in both labels, and the individual faces were dial-for-dial the same at f001, f049 and f097. Confidence is plus or minus one on the absolute integer; confidence that the two labels are EQUAL is high.

Q3 is the only separator, and it is on the standing centre figure at f097. In B the figure holds a clean clothed profile at 12x: jaw, neck, a distinct collar/lapel step at the shoulder, a smooth jacket front and a visible hem above the trousers. In A the same figure at the same zoom has lost the jacket silhouette entirely and the arm has merged into the chest as a single rounded lump with no elbow, no forearm and no hand terminating anywhere, plus a small spur at the jaw/neck junction. Both labels held this figure cleanly at f049, so the failure is specifically late-clip. That is the thing under test.

I am calling the margin marginal rather than clear because the counts differ by exactly one on one question on one frame, and because at native 1x A's figure reads plausibly as a man with folded arms; the absence of any arm structure only becomes unmistakable at 6x and above.

Q4: both fail equally at f097. Measured by best-fit scale search against the reference, both push in roughly 10 percent by the last frame (A 1.095x, B 1.115x) with f001 locked at 1.000x and f049 under 1 percent. A is two points less pushed, which is camera motion rather than coherence and I give it no weight.

Q5: zero hallucinated objects in all six frames. I specifically checked the pair of distant end-of-room lamps, which remain two separate lights in both labels at f097 (an apparent merge in A was an artifact of my own brightness-boosted composite and did not survive an unenhanced zoom), plus the pendant lamp chain, the wall panels and the chairs.

Frame 001 is effectively identical between the two labels (same shared start), and frame 049 is structurally indistinguishable: 6 coherent figures, 0 defects, 0 hallucinations, same dial layout in both. Mean frame luminance at f097 is 54.9 (X) vs 55.1 (Y), so exposure/warmth is not a factor here and no taste axis was in play.

The single separating count is Q3 at frame 097, on the standing man in the centre aisle. In X_f097 he holds his form: a distinct suit-jacket front edge and hem, a separable arm, a defined waist, and a clean profile with nose and chin - verified on raw unenhanced 8x pixels, not just on brightened crops. In Y_f097 that same figure has gone smooth: the jacket has no hem or front edge left, the folded arm reads as a rounded lobe that merges into the chest with no elbow, forearm or hand, the torso runs as one undifferentiated convex mass with no waist, and the jaw blends into the neck. I score that as one structural defect (upper-body melt / limb fused into torso). Legs and shoes are comparable in both, so I did not count a second defect there. This degradation is absent from Y_f049, so it is specifically a late-frame failure, which is the thing under test.

Everything else ties. Both labels keep all six figures (two foreground operators, one mid-left operator, one seated figure behind a chair, one right-mid seated figure, one standing man). Neither fuses a person into a chair; the foreground operators at f097 are clean in both, and Y's right foreground operator is if anything slightly crisper. Neither hallucinated a prop: four ceiling pendants, the same wall panels and chairs as the reference, no additions. Framing drift is identical in both - the back-wall light centroid moves from x=420.6 at f001 to x=433.3 (X) / x=434.3 (Y) at f097, a ~13 px pan on an 832 px frame with no scale change - so Q4 cannot separate them and I scored both YES.

I answered UNKNOWN on Q2 rather than produce a number I cannot defend: the right-hand bank recedes to a vanishing point where the dials compress into an unresolvable string, and that is true of the reference conditioning still as well. What I can say reliably is that the near, large lower-row faces (about 10 in every frame) have distinct rims with dark gaps between them in both labels at f097 - no dials merged into each other in either render.

X wins, but only by that one defect on one figure in one frame, so the honest margin is marginal, not clear.

At the early frame (f049) the two labels are indistinguishable on every countable question: both figure crops show the standing man plus two seated background operators (3 coherent outlines), both dial crops show the same regular bank with no merging, framing matches the reference in both, and neither adds an object. The only f049 difference is overall tone, which I disregarded per instruction.

At the LAST frame (f097) the two separate. In Q_f097_figure I can still resolve three coherent human outlines: the standing man, a seated operator at the left desk with a distinct head above the chair back, and a seated operator leaning at the right console. In P_f097_figure only two survive - the standing man and the right-hand seated operator; the left-hand background operator that was clearly present at f049 no longer reads as a person, its head has gone and the shape collapses into the chair back. I scored that as one structural defect for P (person dissolved into chair) and as the reason its coherent-figure count drops from 3 to 2. Supporting the same direction, the standing man's head profile in Q_f097 keeps a separated nose, chin and jaw-to-neck notch, while in P_f097 the jaw merges into the neck and the head reads flatter and more featureless than the same head did in P_f049. That is a shape difference, not a tonal one.

Dial counts: I answered UNKNOWN for all four cells rather than guess. The crops are small enough that I cannot commit to an exact integer for the front row of the right-hand bank without inventing a number. What I can say reliably is that the dial banks are equally intact in both labels at both frames - rims stay separated, the row spacing stays regular, and I saw no dials merging into one another in any of the four dial crops, so the dial axis contributes nothing to the verdict either way.

Framing was locked to the reference scale and position in all four cells; both labels show the same modest push-in of the console bank between f049 and f097, so no framing penalty applies to either. No hallucinated objects in any cell.

Verdict: Q, but marginal. The two late-frame observations that favour Q (the surviving left operator and the better-held head profile) are visible at native scale rather than only under flipping, but they amount to essentially one dissolving background figure plus one softening face on a single frame, and my chair-versus-person read on the small left background shape carries real uncertainty. That is not enough to call a clear or large margin.

Frame 001 of the two labels is effectively identical (same counts on every question), which confirms a shared start. The labels separate from f049 onward and the gap is widest at the last frame, which is the thing under test.

Q1 (faces). Counting rule I applied: a face counts if an eye and nose are readable and the head silhouette is intact; loss of the mouth line I recorded as degradation rather than disqualification; a head reduced to a featureless blob or with a broken silhouette does not count. Both start at 10. By f097 A holds 5 and B holds 9. In A_f097 the mid-left redhead's jaw silhouette has broken into a stepped, notched polygon with the mouth erased; the grey-haired man beside him has his profile fused into the head in front; the mid-right man's eye has become a featureless black rounded slab with the mouth gone; the right-hand redhead carries two separate dark marks on the face (a large black oval plus a second smudge at the nose position). The same figures in B_f097 keep smooth continuous profiles with eye, nose and a mouth line.

Q4 (structural defects). A: 0 / 3 / 5. The clearest one is the back-crowd pair at top right. In A_f001 that is a black-haired man with a readable ear and jaw plus a grey-haired man with eye and nose. By A_f049 a pale streaked tendril has grown between the two heads and the grey-haired man's face is gone; by A_f097 the black-haired head is an amorphous black mass with pale finger-like protrusions emerging from it and the neighbouring head is a lumpy featureless polygon. B: 0 / 1 / 1, the single defect being that same far-right background head going featureless; the near-black-haired man's ear and jaw stay intact in B at both later frames.

Q5 (hallucinated objects). A_f049 and A_f097 both carry a bright yellow-white dot with a dark ring beside it on the ear of the right-hand foreground figure; nothing like it exists in the reference or in A_f001. A_f097 adds a second one: a glowing filament-shaped object behind the leftmost tube, against a cabinet wall that is plain in A_f001. B shows neither, at either later frame, and its tube bay wall stays plain.

Q3 (tubes). 6 separate intact tubes in the reference and in all six frames. No separation on this question.

Q2 (ticks). I could not count the full scale reliably at 832x480 - the fine hatch along the left half of the arc reads as a bead texture, not as separable strokes, so the whole-scale count is UNKNOWN for every frame. I counted instead over a scene-defined span, from the red pointer to the right end of the arc, which is comparable across frames regardless of framing. A: 9 / 6 / 10. B: 9 / 9 / 15. I discount part of B's f097 advantage: the camera pushes in slightly on B so the meter occupies more pixels, and A_f049's dip is partly reduced contrast on a brighter meter face. This question is the weakest evidence of the five and I would not decide on it alone.

Caveat I want on the record: B's late frames are framed slightly closer, so its crowd faces are roughly 10-15 percent larger on screen. That scale difference could flatter B on face legibility. It does not explain the findings I actually leaned on, which are structural and scale-independent: a jaw silhouette broken into a notched polygon, a head fused with finger shapes, duplicated eye marks, and a persistent invented bright dot. Those appear in A and not in B. The differences are visible at normal viewing size, not only by flipping at high zoom, so I call the margin clear rather than marginal - but not large, since A_f097 still reads as a coherent picture at a glance and the invented dot is small.

Counting rule for Q1: I counted only the nine near-field heads large enough for structural coherence to be testable (left foreground head, far-left partial face, dark-haired man upper-left, red-haired man left-of-centre, pale-haired man left-of-centre, two right-band profiles, right-band redhead, right foreground head). Everything deeper in the hall is a faceless silhouette in the reference itself, so it cannot be scored as erased. f001 is pixel-identical between the two labels (9/9), confirming the shared start.

Q1: both labels end the clip at 8 of 9, but for different reasons, and that difference is the finding. In X the right-foreground figure rotates away between f001 and f049, so no face is exposed there at f049 or f097; the back of the head and the ear are cleanly drawn (crop of x680-832 at 6x). In Y that figure keeps facing camera, but by f049 its eye has stopped being an eye: the reference and both f001 frames show a normal white sclera with a dark pupil under a drawn brow, and Y_f049/Y_f097 show an angular black wedge with no sclera and no brow. That is a degraded face, not a rotation, and it persists unchanged to the last frame. All other eight near-field faces hold in both labels, including both large foreground heads, which are clean in X_f097 and Y_f097 alike.

Q2: answered UNKNOWN for all six frames rather than guessed. The scale is drawn as irregular sketchy strokes that merge into a hatch band; at 8x and 13x I could not resolve a repeatable count of separate ticks in any frame, including f001. Qualitatively both labels still carry a tick band at f097 - X_f097 keeps a slightly finer hatch and a visibly dotted arc line while Y_f097 is softer with a smooth arc - but that is a sharpness impression, not a countable difference, so it does not move the verdict.

Q3: 6 tubes in every frame of both labels (large left, two mediums, the tall narrow one standing behind, the small front-right, large right), all outlines closed and separate. No merging, no loss. Straight tie.

Q4/Q5: the one real asymmetry. In Y_f049 and Y_f097 the ear region of the right-foreground figure has collapsed into a bright cream disc joined by a thin stem to a dark grey oval - it reads as a metal pin or tack, and there is nothing like it in the reference, where that area is a plain drawn ear with a partially visible head behind it. I scored the lost eye as the structural defect and the disc/stem/oval as the hallucinated object, so they are counted once each rather than twice. I noticed the bright dot on the first native-resolution pass before any zoom, which is why I did not treat it as a flip-at-high-zoom difference. X shows neither artefact in any frame.

Things I deliberately did not score: the tuning knob takes a mauve/violet sheen in both labels at f049 (Y's is more saturated), so it is a colour/saturation difference and excluded per the brief; Y_f097's meter face is darker and X_f097's is brighter and more washed out, also excluded; and the extra dark mark beside the right-band redhead's nose is present in the shared f001 and in the reference, so it is inherited, not a new doubled eye - I checked that specifically before discarding it. Y_f097 is also globally softer than X_f097 in the mid-crowd, which supports X but is not one of the counted questions.

Margin is "clear" rather than "large": every counted quantity except defects and hallucinations is a tie, and the difference is one figure out of nine. It is not "marginal" because the defect is visible without flipping or zooming, is a specific named failure (an eye replaced by a black wedge, an ear replaced by an object), appears on both late frames rather than flickering, and is exactly the late-frame coherence property under test.

Q1/Q4 carry the verdict. Both crops show the same three foreground heads (a near-profile head at left, a head in the middle, and a larger three-quarter head at right) in front of a defocused crowd. In P, at BOTH frame 049 and frame 097, all three foreground faces carry a full feature set: brow, eye (two eyes on the right-hand three-quarter head), a nose that reads as a distinct bump on the silhouette with a nostril mark, a mouth line, and a defined chin. In Q, at BOTH frames, the left and middle foreground faces have an eye and nothing else - the silhouette runs straight where the nose should protrude and there is no mouth line at all; the right-hand face keeps two eyes and a mouth but its nose is flattened out of the silhouette. That is 3 coherent faces for P versus 1 for Q at each frame, and 3 feature-erasure defects for Q at each frame versus 0 for P.

I specifically tested whether this was just an exposure/contrast difference, since Q renders those two heads darker. Grayscale + autocontrast normalisation of the identical region in both labels still shows the nose bump, mouth notch and chin crease in P and still shows blank ovals with a single eye in Q. So it is missing geometry, not missing light. This is visible in the plain 4x views and is discernible in the native crops, so it is not a high-zoom-only artefact.

On the last frame specifically (rule 8): P holds all three faces at f097 exactly as it did at f049; Q holds one at f097 exactly as it did at f049. Neither label DEGRADES across the clip - both are stable frame to frame - but P is carrying substantially more intact facial structure at the late frame.

Q2 I am answering UNKNOWN honestly for all four. The meter scale is drawn as a fine hatch chain running along the arc plus taller ticks rising above it; at native resolution the fine hatch merges into the arc line in places and my count would swing by several either way, so I will not state an integer. What I can report without guessing a number is the ordering of articulation: P frame 097 shows the densest and most separated hatch along the whole arc, P frame 049 close behind, Q frame 097 sparser, and Q frame 049 the softest - in Q frame 049 much of the left-hand hatch has smoothed into a plain dark line. So the tick evidence points the same way as the faces, but I am not converting it into counts.

Q3 is not answerable from this material: neither the faces crop nor the meter crop contains the tube bay. The faces crop stops at the glowing cabinet top and the antenna base; the meter crop shows the meter glass, bezel and tuning knob. No glass tube appears in any of the eight files, for either label.

Q5: 0 for all four. I found nothing I could confidently call an object absent from the reference. The one candidate was a saturated orange disc at the right edge of Q frame 097 beside the front head, but the same area in Q frame 049 reads as that figure's rim-lit ear, and the reference hall is full of warm-lit heads, so I am not counting it.

Margin is "clear" rather than "large": the difference is real, repeated across two faces and both frames, and survives normalisation, but nothing in either render is grossly melted, both keep the same composition and pose, and Q's degraded faces are still sane head shapes rather than streaks.

Every legibility instrument ties on every matched frame. Both labels start identical to the reference at f001 (eye chart row 5 legible on both panels, shape row 4 identifiable on both panels, gratings striped down to the 3px group, 8 colour bars, no artifacts). Both degrade in exactly the same way by f049: eye chart row 5 (KNORSV) collapses into a smear on both panels for both labels while row 4 (VZCDH) survives, the 3px grating group turns into an aliased block on both panels for both labels while 4px stays separated, shape rows 1-4 hold, and both labels grow the SAME large blue-cyan blob in the right half of the dark eye-chart panel. Nothing separates them through f049.

The only separation is the artifact count on the last frame, and it is one item. A f097: the blue blob has grown (roughly x570-815, y265-415, up from x615-790, y288-390 at f049) and a distinct smaller circular lobe has budded off its left edge - 2 countable artifacts. The rest of A's card stays near-reference in colour: the dark grating strip is still neutral cream/grey and the colour-bar row is clean. B f097: the blue blob has SHRUNK (roughly x650-770, y305-370, smaller than its own f049 state, and clearly smaller than A's), which is a point in B's favour, but three other countable artifacts appear that A does not have - the entire dark grating strip has lost its neutral colour and rendered in strong blue/yellow/cyan casts, the top colour-bar row has smeared with pink/lavender patches over its right end, and a yellow-orange crescent has appeared at the far left of the light shapes panel overlapping the row-1 circle. That is 3 countable artifacts against A's 2.

So the vote is A by one item on one question (Q7, last frame only), and it is a genuine trade: B's primary blob is smaller and better contained late, A's card holds its colour and its grating strip late. I did not score brightness, contrast, warmth or saturation. None of the colour contamination on B reduced grating SEPARATION or bar COUNT, so Q5, Q6 and Q8 remain tied at 4/4/8. Q1-Q4 are tied at every frame for both labels. Anyone counting artifact AREA rather than artifact COUNT would land on B or on TIE, which is why I am calling the margin marginal rather than clear.

Seven of the eight asked questions are dead-equal across every frame for both labels. Q1/Q2: both start at row 5 fully legible at f001, both lose row 5 (the K and N of KNORSV merge into one mark) by f049 and never recover it, and both still read VZCDH cleanly on light and dark at f097 - so 5/5/4/4/4/4 identically for X and Y. Q3/Q4: shape row 4 (diamond, plus, circle, square, triangle) stays identifiable on both panels in all six frames - 4 everywhere. Q5/Q6: the 3px grating keeps visibly separated bars in every frame on both panels; I measured mean modulation depth over the 3px group and it never drops below 174 of 255 (X f049 light, the worst cell), so 3 everywhere. Q8: all 8 bars present and distinct in every frame - I sampled bar centres and every one stays unambiguously white/yellow/cyan/green/magenta/red/blue/black, although X f097 has pushed red toward orange (220,88,58 vs Y 219,52,45) and warped the red/blue boundary into a slant.

The only asked question that separates them is Q7 at the last frame, and it separates them by one, in opposite directions depending on whether you count instances or size. By COUNT X f097 is worse: four discrete hallucinations (the blue blob in the dark eye-chart panel; a yellow-olive smear fused to the left side of the row-1 circle on the light shapes panel; a pale-yellow rectangular patch at the top of the light eye-chart panel; a pink/magenta patch in the greyscale ramp near the right end). Y f097 has three (the blue blob, now with a round satellite lobe attached on its left; a dark round smudge in the upper right of the dark shapes panel; the same pale-yellow patch, fainter). By SIZE Y f097 is worse, and by a lot: thresholding the dark eye-chart panel at luminance 60, the blob measures 6,515 px in X f097 against 26,861 px in Y f097 - roughly four times the area - and Y's mass has grown from 12,103 px at f049 while X's shrank from 16,865 px. Y's blob at f097 also spills upward past the panel edge into the grating strip. So on the specific late-frame-coherence question the count says Y and the magnitude says X, and they cancel. One further countable fact I did not weigh into the verdict because it is not among the eight questions: X f097's neutral greyscale ramp has gone strongly non-neutral (mean channel spread 12.87, max 57, against Y's 2.23/26) and its blank light eye-chart panel is about three times more mottled (luminance std 1.28, range 19, against Y's 0.56, range 4). I could not count that as blobs without double-counting the smears already listed.

Every countable instrument reading is IDENTICAL between P and Q at both frames. Eye chart: rows 1-4 (C / DHK / NORS / VZCDH) are fully legible on both light and dark panels in all eight eye crops; row 5 (KNORSV) is a blurred smear in all eight and is never fully legible. So Q1 and Q2 are 4 across the board. Gratings: all six groups (16, 12, 8, 6, 4, 3px) still show discretely separated bars in all eight grating crops, on both panels and both frames, for both labels - so Q5 and Q6 are 3 across the board. The two labels are indistinguishable on legibility.

The single countable difference is Q7 on the DARK eye panel at the LATE frame. Both renders hallucinate the same thing at f049: one glowing blue rounded-rectangle "screen" occupying the right half of the dark eye panel, which does not exist in the reference (reference dark eye panel is plain black with white letters and row numerals). P=1, Q=1 at f049 - a tie, and the two f049 dark crops are near twins.

At f097 they diverge. P's blob is still ONE object: it holds a defined rounded-rectangle boundary with a crisp dark surround, essentially the same shape it had at f049. Q's blob has bloomed into a large diffuse oval with a soft halo spilling well past its edge, AND has shed a SECOND, separate small round blue-grey blob sitting clearly detached to its left at about row-2 height. That satellite is present in Q_f097_eye_dark and absent in Q_f049_eye_dark, P_f049_eye_dark and P_f097_eye_dark. P=1, Q=2.

Supporting (not one of the eight counted questions, so it does not change the margin): in Q_f097_eye_dark the right-edge row numerals 1-5 are washed to near-invisibility by the milky lift, while in P_f097_eye_dark they remain readable. That is consistent with the same late-frame drift, not an independent finding.

Q3, Q4 and Q8 are UNKNOWN for every label and frame because no shapes panel and no colour-bar strip appear anywhere in the sixteen crops supplied - only eye-chart and grating panels were cropped. I did not guess those.

Verdict: P, by exactly one count on exactly one question (Q7, dark panel, late frame only). Everything else ties. Both renders differ in warmth, contrast and chroma fringing, which I ignored per instruction. Margin is marginal, not clear - the satellite blob is visible at native scale, but it is a one-count edge on a single question and P and Q are otherwise dead level.
